maria: Quick flag — noticed a token-level latency bump on the nightly FP8->INT4 rollout when KV cache hits dip under ~70%. p50 flat, p95 up ~6%, p99 up ~12%. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
raj: I saw a smaller bump in my traces. Does this correlate with kernel switching (fp8->int4) or batching amplification when cache misses force more compute?
taylor: Posting a short trace: perf-bot nightly job shows kernel_counters flipping to int4 on layer 10 onward when calibration fallback triggers. Might be the kernel selection threshold is too eager.
perf-bot: nightly-run: model=redwood-small-ctx2k, workload=chatbox, sample=5000 tokens, cache_hit_rate=68.2%, mean_token_latency_ms=12.8, p95=28.3, p99=42.6. kernel_profile: {fp8_calls: 11200, int4_calls: 8200, fp8_avg_ms:0.9, int4_avg_ms:1.6} :chart_with_upwards_trend:
olivia: Interesting that int4_avg_ms is higher — expected lower. Could be quantization-dequantization or mixed-precision conversion overhead killing vectorized kernels when interleaved.
raj: Can you paste the kernel counters + batching histogram? We need to see if int4 kernels are getting tiny micro-batches due to batching heuristics when cache misses cause spike in seq-len or kv behavior.
maria: Here's a small snippet from the trace collector (simplified):
```
kernel_counter: fp8_kernel calls=11200 time_ns=10080000000
kernel_counter: int4_kernel calls=8200 time_ns=13120000000
batch_size_hist: 1:4200, 2:3300, 4:1800, 8+:2800
kv_cache_hits: 68.2%
prefix_cache_lookups: 14300
```
taylor: That `int4_kernel time_ns` >> `calls` suggests per-call overhead is big. Looks like int4 path has an extra copy/transpose or slower GEMM. Also notice many batch_size=1 calls — tiny batches amplify overhead.
olivia: Could also be kernel selection causing frequent fallbacks between fp8 and int4 per-layer (selector instability). If selector is per-layer + per-token, and cache misses change sequence lengths, we might be thrashing kernels mid-request.
raj: Agreed. Two hypotheses: 1) Kernel selector uses a heuristic based on per-layer activation stats that becomes noisy when kv misses occur; when it flips we pay conversion cost. 2) Batching heuristic doesn't coalesce micro-batches for int4 (e.g., alignment constraints). We should validate both.
calib-bot: calib-check: recent calibration run for model=redwood-small-ctx2k shows int4 accuracy delta -0.6% vs fp8 baseline on holdout prompts, but variance high on long-seq prompts.
maria: Plan: add a probe to trace selector decisions and per-token kernel tags, plus batch coalescing tags. If we can confirm selector flips within the same request, that's a smoking gun.
taylor: I'll add `selector_trace` with entries like `layer,chosen_kernel,reason,seq_len_snapshot` to the per-request span. Example: `10,int4,expected_mem_saving,256`
raj: Also capture `post-selector` micro-batch sizes and alignment pads. Maybe int4 kernel needs 128-aligned inputs and small batches cause scalar path.
perf-bot: quick query I ran across recent traces: average number of selector switches per request = 1.9 (stdev 1.3) when cache_hit_rate < 75%, vs 0.4 when cache_hit_rate >= 75%.
olivia: That metric nails it. Selector is noisy under cache churn. We should consider stabilizing the selector: hysteresis (stay on kernel X for N layers), or prefer fp8 on boundary cases to avoid conversion thrash.
maria: For a quick mitigation, can we flip default preference to FP8 when cache_hit_rate < 80%? Might raise compute cost but reduce p99 tail. We need an A/B to measure cost vs latency.
raj: Let's run an experiment: route 10% of traffic with `selector_policy=prefer_fp8_on_low_cache` and compare latency + cost. Add observability: per-token kernel tag, and counters for `conversion_ops` (bytes copied for quant/dequant).
taylor: I'll draft the canary config and the additional tracing fields. Also instrument batching: `microbatch_coalesced=true/false` flag per kernel call.
perf-bot: scheduled-job: run canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC for 2 hours, sample=10k tokens, metrics exported to /shared/perf/1965552222/canary.
maria: One more ask — add a per-token latency breakdown in traces: `decode_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_exec_ms, quant_conversion_ms, copy_ms`. Right now we only have kernel_exec aggregated.
olivia: Agreed. That breakdown will show if quant conversion is the dominant extra cost. If conversion_ms >> kernel_exec_ms for int4, we need to optimize conversion or avoid switching.
raj: FYI I'm going to check kernel implementations for extra memcpy or suboptimal int4 GEMM path. If we find a fast path (fused dequant+gemm), we can reduce conversion_ms significantly.
taylor: Will update the selector to respect a min_stability_layers param (default 2) so we don't flip every layer. We'll push the trace changes first.
maria: Thanks all — action items: taylor add traces + canary config; raj audit int4 kernel; olivia run cost-latency trade analysis for prefer_fp8_on_low_cache; perf-bot run canary tomorrow.
raj: Also adding an alert: if avg selector switches per request > 1 and p99 latency increases > 5% over baseline, page the runtime-oncall.
maria: OK closing the loop — keep updates in this thread. :white_check_mark:
